Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-u27i64wl/call-ebaf628e42d54482bfcaff3cf8ea63de/manuscript.pdf

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
p=Path('tmp/pdfs'); p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages):
 text=page.extract_text()
 (p/f'page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(text)
 print(f'\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n{text}')
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from itertools import product
# Two layers a -> b, two nonempty stages, one strategy per layer.
for placement in [(0,1),(1,0)]:
 P=[[int(placement[u]==i) for i in range(2)] for u in range(2)]
 feasible_z=[]
 for vals in product([0,1],repeat=4):
  Z=[list(vals[:2]),list(vals[2:])]
  if all(Z[u][i]>=P[u][i] for u in range(2) for i in range(2)) and all(Z[1][i]<=Z[0][i] and Z[1][i]<=P[1][i]-P[0][i]+1 for i in range(2)):
   feasible_z.append(Z)
 # Unit compute cost, cross-stage resharding cost 10, two microbatches.
 p=[sum(P[u][i] for u in range(2)) for i in range(2)]
 o=P[0][0]*P[1][1]*10
 objective=sum(p)+o+max(p+[o])
 print({'stage_a':placement[0]+1,'stage_b':placement[1]+1,'feasible_Z':feasible_z,'Eq4_communication':o,'Eq2_objective':objective})
PY"

strengths: UniAP addresses a useful infrastructure problem with direct relevance to training large vision models. Combining pipeline placement with layer-specific DP, TP, and FSDP choices provides a coherent way to account for communication, computation, and memory tradeoffs.

Table 2 reports meaningful measured throughput improvements. On ENVB, ViT-Huge reaches 45.58 samples/s versus 38.74 for Alpa and 32.20 for Galvatron; Swin-Huge improves from 13.90 to 19.08 samples/s over Galvatron. LLaMA also shows a substantial 1.61× improvement.

Reduced planning time is a valuable contribution even where training throughput ties the strongest baseline. For example, on ENVA, BERT-Huge matches Galvatron's throughput while reducing reported strategy optimization time from 6.44 to 0.37 minutes.

The evaluation covers five models and several hardware configurations. The reported 3.59% average throughput estimation error supports the cost model's practical usefulness on the evaluated solutions. Hardware descriptions, solver settings, and the topology-aware case study help readers understand the system.
weaknesses: The published constraints do not ensure the pipeline ordering required by the communication model. For a two-layer chain u→v, placing u on stage 2 and v on stage 1 satisfies the contiguity and placement constraints, but Equation (4) counts no communication for that edge because it only includes transfers from stage j to j+1. Thus, the objective can favor an assignment with omitted communication costs. Appendix A proves contiguity, not stage ordering. This is a material correctness gap in the central formulation, and the manuscript does not document additional implementation constraints that resolve it.

The claimed MIQP is not quadratic as written: Equations (3) and (4) contain products of four binary variables, such as P_ui P_vi S_uk S_vl. Auxiliary variables could provide an equivalent reformulation, but that formulation and its linking constraints are absent. This is a repairable specification issue, yet it prevents reproducing and checking the actual optimization problem passed to Gurobi.

The repeated optimality claims exceed the evidence. Appendix D allows termination after 60 seconds and early termination with a remaining optimality gap below 4%, but achieved gaps are not reported. Moreover, optimization uses estimated costs and a restricted configuration enumeration. The complexity argument in Section 3.5 treats solver time as a fixed budget; it does not establish the time required to obtain an optimal solution. These distinctions affect a central claimed advantage over prior methods.

The experiments do not isolate the benefit of joint optimization over hierarchical optimization. Figure 7 removes an entire category of parallelism, demonstrating the usefulness of combining categories rather than the superiority of the proposed search formulation. A hierarchical comparison using the same cost model and candidate strategies is absent. Hierarchical decomposition is not inherently suboptimal, and the manuscript also identifies improved cost estimation and multithreaded solving as contributors to its gains.

Validation establishes narrower practical benefits than some conclusions suggest. Cost accuracy is evaluated only on selected solutions, so candidate-ranking accuracy remains untested. Figure 5 increases batch size with node count and reaches only 16 GPUs, supporting limited weak-scaling evidence rather than a general solver scalability claim. Reported optimization times exclude profiling, leaving total preparation overhead unquantified. These limitations are secondary; the unresolved formulation and optimality issues determine the weak-reject recommendation despite the worthwhile measured gains.
